memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "But the goat chosen by lot as the scapegoat shall be presented alive before the LORD to be used for making atonement by sending it into the wilderness as a scapegoat." - Lev 16:10 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Presented alive. That is the detail that stops you.

The other goat dies at the altar. This one stands there breathing, alive, waiting — and its fate is not death but exile. It will be led out into the wilderness and released where no one lives, and it will never come back.

Where does our sin go? That is the question this goat answers. Not filed away. Not suspended pending review. Sent away, into a place from which it does not return.

David wrote as far as the east is from the west, so far has he removed our transgressions from us (Ps 103:12). East and west never meet. There is no point at which they converge.

Micah pictured it differently: you will tread our sins underfoot and hurl all our iniquities into the depths of the sea (Mic 7:19). Hurled. Not placed carefully at the shoreline where the tide might return them.

Many believers live as though their sins were merely relocated somewhere nearby, ready to be produced again. They confess the same thing repeatedly, never quite believing it has gone.

Watch the goat disappear over the horizon. That is what God has done with what you brought Him.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Do you believe your confessed sin is truly gone, or just filed away?
2. What sin do you keep retrieving that God has already sent away?
3. How would today feel if you truly believed it was removed?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, thank You that You do not merely file my sin away but send it away entirely. Help me stop retrieving what You have removed as far as the east is from the west. Amen.
